Cause: The accounts-api 3.1.0 image removed the legacy /healthz endpoint and split health into /livez and /readyz (per the pod's own startup logs: "health endpoints moved to the standard split: /livez, /readyz (legacy /healthz removed, see CHANGELOG 3.1.0)"). The Deployment's readiness probe still targets GET /healthz on :8080, so the kubelet gets HTTP 404 on every probe ("Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 404", repeated in logs as "GET /healthz 404 ua=kube-probe"). A failing readiness probe keeps the Pod's Ready condition false, so it never receives traffic and the rollout cannot progress past the first new replica [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/probes#configure-probes-2] [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#readiness-probe-0]. Stuck rollouts due to readiness probe failures are a documented Deployment failure mode [cite: concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment#failed-deployment-0].

Evidence:
- New pod accounts-api-8f4b6d7c9-m7zjn (image 3.1.0): ready=false, message "Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 404".
- Pod logs show the app is up and listening on :8080 serving /livez, /readyz, /metrics; probes to /healthz return 404.
- Old 3.0.4 pods (which do expose /healthz) are Ready and still serving — consistent with the probe path, not the app, being the problem.

Fix (for the Deployment owner to apply): Update the accounts-api Deployment's readinessProbe (and livenessProbe, if it also points at /healthz) to use the new endpoints — httpGet.path: /readyz for readinessProbe and /livez for livenessProbe, port 8080 — then re-apply. The new pod should go Ready within a probe period or two and the rolling update will continue, retiring the old 3.0.4 replicas. No cluster-side change is needed.

Side note (not part of this ticket): accounts-worker-55d8b9c6f-rk2tv has 2 restarts with last state Terminated exit code 1 — worth a separate look if it keeps recurring.
